channel.title: Liuwa Pod
channel.description: Liuwa Pod takes the world apart every morning, from Lusaka. In about eighteen minutes: the biggest stories in the world overnight and what they mean for the price of power, fuel, food and money in Zambia; one mechanism taken apart properly; where AI, space, chips, software and cyber security are going; one page of knowledge explained from the ground up; one step of maths a day, building one idea across the week; and a word and a day from history. Lombe, Mwila, K.B. and Professor Mulenga are fictional hosts with synthetic voices; every figure is sourced in the show notes and independently checked. Nothing on Liuwa Pod is financial advice. Made by Liuwa Tech.

item.title: Ep 25 · Huang walks out of Nvidia, and the sun gets stored for the evening
item.description:
Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's chief executive, and we take apart how a US chip export licence works and how controlled chips still leak through third countries. Also: Brent back near $96 on claimed Gulf attacks, US envoys in Moscow, yields near 5%. Then Gemini 4 Hydrogen, an Apache patch to run today, the merit order, and a battery that stores the sun for Lusaka's evening.

item.description:

Parliament has an extra K19.9bn budget for 2026, mostly to pay farmers who sold maize to the FRA, and the 2027 budget is reported for Friday: how the maize bill grew, who wins and who pays, and why government borrowing can make a shop loan dearer. item.description:

Oil has its third straight weekly gain and its highest close since April, so we separate what is confirmed in the Gulf from what is only claimed and look at what it means for the fuel review due around 31 Oct. Professor Mumba brings the word asunder, an Olympic twist from 1964, and a sum in which the last doubling beats all the earlier ones.
